title: Gate audio playback and input on renderer readiness

title: Show difficulty-accurate timing windows on the note runway
description: Add a bounded gameplay UI feature, separately authorized after the approved per-song difficulty profiles: make the active run's actual Perfect and Good timing tolerance visible in two matching places: each falling note has a vertical Good envelope with a smaller Perfect core, and the fixed target at the hit line has matching Good/Perfect bands. This is related to the previously resolved timing-window discussion (shining-stars-4v0.10) but does not reopen it or alter timing, chart notes, note speed, scoring, calibration, or difficulty rules. Notes stop at the hit line during late grace; the paired visualization and copy must show that the fixed bands mark the target and the note envelopes show its timing tolerance, not a path of continued travel beyond the line. Use the active run's frozen difficulty profile, not the next-run selector. Derive geometry from the rendered runway's actual pixels-per-second with responsive sizing. Preserve current lane layout and note appearance outside this scope. Good is the outer envelope/band and Perfect its distinct nested core. Do not inflate accurate geometry to satisfy minimum visibility; use an outline or label. Provide accessible text/semantics and respect reduced-motion; no motion is required. No generic redesign or reusable effects framework.
design: Represent the same timing interval on both the moving note and the fixed hit target: for a timing window of ±W seconds and rendered runway speed S pixels/second, target bands extend W×S above and below the hit line; a falling-note envelope is 2W×S tall and centered on its note. The inner Perfect geometry nests in the outer Good geometry. These are two depictions of one acceptance window, not extra time or a new mechanic. Keep the current hit-line-centered clamp: notes stop at the line during late grace. Explain that the bands are a centered timing target, not a path notes travel through. Derive S from current responsive runway travel distance and the existing approach duration, not a hard-coded CSS size. Supply the profile from game.difficulty, frozen for the run, never the next-run selector. Ensure fixed bands and moving envelopes share geometry/data and active profile. If tiny Hard geometry needs minimum visibility, retain true measurements and add a non-misleading outline/label.
acceptance_criteria: 1. During an active run, each falling note shows an outer Good timing envelope with a distinct nested Perfect core, and the fixed hit-line target shows matching Good/Perfect bands derived from the same active-run profile and shared geometry; changing the next-run selection cannot alter the current visualization. 2. For a ±W-second window and measured runway speed S pixels/second, fixed bands extend W×S on either side of the hit line and note envelopes are 2W×S tall. Easy Good (±500ms) is five times Hard Good (±100ms) at equal scale; responsive runway changes scale proportionally. 3. Hit-line origin and note approach/clamp behavior remain unchanged. Copy distinguishes fixed target bands from note travel and does not imply notes pass through the line or that the two depictions add timing tolerance. 4. Preserve existing lane geometry; desktop/narrow layouts stay usable. Perfect/Good are distinct without color alone, accessible text/semantics are legible, reduced motion is respected, and minimum-visibility treatments do not falsify scale. 5. Tests cover Easy/Normal/Hard Good and Perfect geometry, nested bands/envelopes, responsive scale, and use of frozen active profile for both depictions. Browser verification covers desktop and narrow layout. No timing/scoring/chart/calibration/transport changes.
notes: Implementation added the shared profile-aware geometry in src/note-projection.ts and rendered both moving-note envelopes and fixed hit-line bands in src/ui.ts/src/styles.css. Uses game.difficulty frozen in the run and measured lane-board clientHeight × 0.64, observed with ResizeObserver (window resize fallback), disposed with UI. 2026-10-09: focused regressions now cover all three profiles, Easy/Normal/Hard ratios (5×, 1.5×), Good/Perfect geometry, responsive scaling, shared target/note source, and frozen-profile source. Full verification: 179 Vitest passed; typecheck, lint, format:check, build, chart:check, 48 Python chart tests passed; build only reports existing >500KB JS chunk warning. Chromium screenshots saved outside repo at /tmp/opencode/brightvale-timing-visuals/{desktop.png,mobile.png,hard.png,hard-mobile.png,normal-desktop.png}. Browser checks confirmed Normal desktop Good height 32.625px; Hard desktop 21.75px (2/3 ratio); Hard mobile 18.766px from measured responsive travel height; note-envelope and fixed-target Good heights match exactly. Detector returned no findings. Parent still owns independent GREEN review; do not close before that review.
close_reason: Independent review accepted with no findings. Focused 6/6 and full 179/179 Vitest passed; Python chart suite 48 passed; typecheck, lint, format check, build, chart:check, and diff check passed. Desktop Normal/Hard and 390x844 mobile Chromium geometry verified matching Good/Perfect target and note envelopes, active frozen profile despite opposite next selection, responsive resize, and Hard/Normal ratio 0.6662. Screenshots/evidence: /tmp/opencode/brightvale-timing-visuals-validation/. Owned Vite/browser groups terminated; groups absent and port 5173 listener absent.

title: Implement per-song selectable difficulty profiles
description: Implement user-approved Easy/Normal/Hard profiles for note timing, Audience Renown rewards, and Twilight costs/damage, while keeping the same chart notes across profiles. Canonical values: Easy Perfect +/-0.250s, Good +/-0.500s; Audience P/G/M=2/1/0; Twilight cost P/G/M=0/0/2 and damage=2/1/0. Normal Perfect +/-0.075s, Good +/-0.150s; Audience=3/2/0; Twilight cost=0/1/3 and damage=3/2/0. Hard Perfect +/-0.050s, Good +/-0.100s; Audience=5/3/0; Twilight cost=0/2/3 and damage=5/3/0. Keep each profile's values together in one shared source (proposed canonical JSON data/charts/difficulty-profiles.json consumed by TypeScript and the Python chart workflow; do not duplicate profile constants). Add per-song allowed_difficulties to data/charts/song-authoring.json; current The First Shining Star permits ['normal','hard']. Keep twilight_strength=100 and do not scale enemy strength by difficulty. Default to Normal if allowed, otherwise first declared allowed difficulty; reject empty/unknown/duplicate choices. Freeze chosen profile for a run; difficulty can change only while idle or on results, never during a run or pause. Preserve the current +/-0.200s input-offset limit. Runtime chart guards and aubio generator must use the maximum Good window among the song's allowed profiles plus that offset for start, handoff, and end safety. Current Normal/Hard max Good window is 150ms, so preserve current note timestamps. Update generated artifact/chart and tests/docs only in the implementation phase, after this test-first gate. No installs/downloads.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical profile source defines all timing/reward/cost/damage values and is consumed by game/UI/controller plus chart guard/generator logic. JSON authoring config validates and round-trips allowed_difficulties into the generated playable chart. Current song allows Normal and Hard, keeps Twilight Strength 100 and identical notes. Tests cover exact inclusive timing edges and outside edges for every profile, overlapping-note nearest/tie behavior, audience and combat values/misses, allowed selection/rejection/defaults, run freeze and idle/results-only switching, config validation/round-trip, and chart/generator safety using maximum allowed Good window and +/-200ms offset. Existing timestamps and Normal/Hard behavior remain unchanged; current +/−200ms limit remains. Implementation, independent validation, and review are separately verified before close.

Generator provenance records maximum_allowed_good_window_ms and uses profiles for guards/cache invalidation. Local evidence: 120 focused Vitest and 48 Python tests passed; typecheck/lint/format, chart generate/check passed. Source/lock hashes unchanged; note projection identical at 80 (44 Audience/36 Twilight), Normal/Hard guard max 150ms, Twilight Strength 100. Pending designer-owned consumers: main callback must pass selected difficulty; UI selector/copy/results must use lookup; scene-state response should use selected profile rather than Normal compatibility alias. Final independent verification and review accepted BC-06. GREEN evidence: 173 Vitest and 48 Python tests passed; all quality gates and deterministic chart regeneration passed. Canonical shared profile data: data/charts/difficulty-profiles.json; current-song allowed list: data/charts/song-authoring.json. Chart remains 80 notes and Twilight Strength 100. title: Implement Renown scoring and Twilight strength combat
description: Approved scoring plan: replace Resonance with Renown. Audience outcomes award Miss=0, Good=2, Perfect=3 Renown, without caps/discards. At Twilight entry Personal Strength equals accumulated Renown; Twilight Strength starts at a positive per-song configurable value, initially100. In Twilight Miss costs3 Personal Strength and deals0 damage; Good costs1 Personal Strength and deals2 damage; Perfect costs0 Personal Strength and deals3 damage. Centralize all outcome values in one shared balance configuration used consistently across game; per-song twilight_strength in song-authoring JSON must flow into generated playable chart. Twilight reaching0 means victory; Personal Strength reaching0 means defeat; excerpt ending while both remain above0 means survived but Twilight undefeated.
